name: Poc Chuc (Yucatán-Style Grilled Pork Tacos)

cookwares.name: grill basket or small cast iron skillet (optional)

ingredients.name: thinly sliced boneless pork loin chops

instructions.primary_message: Peel and quarter the yellow onion. Peel the garlic. Stem the habanero.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 medium yellow onion
5 medium cloves garlic
½ to 1 habanero

instructions.primary_message: In a small bowl, whisk together cumin, oregano, clove, and salt. On a wire rack set in a rimmed baking sheet, spread the pork in an even layer. Sprinkle both sides of the pork with the prepared seasoning mixture, gently patting it into the meat to adhere. Refrigerate pork, uncovered, for at least 1 hour and up to 12 hours.

For a Charcoal Grill: Open bottom vent completely. Light large chimney starter, filled with charcoal briquettes (about 6 quarts). When top coals are partially covered with ash, pour evenly over grill grate. Set cooking grate in place, cover, and open lid vent completely. Heat grill until hot, about 5 minutes.
For a Gas Grill: Turn all burners to high, cover, and heat grill until hot, about 15 minutes. Leave burners on high.

Clean and oil the cooking grate. Place onion, garlic, and habaneros on the grill. (If needed, use a grill basket or small cast iron skillet to prevent onion, garlic, and habaneros from falling through grates.) Cook, flipping occasionally, until charred all over, about 8 minutes. Transfer to a blender. Add grapefruit, orange, and lime juice to blender. Blend on high speed until smooth, about 1 minute. Season with salt to taste. Set aside.

Place pork chops on heated grill and cook (covered if using gas), flipping chops once about halfway through, until browned on both sides and just cooked through, 2 to 4 minutes per side. Transfer to a cutting board.
Cut pork into 1.5-cm square pieces. Transfer diced pork to a large bowl. Add 1/2 cup of the reserved citrus salsa and toss until meat is thoroughly coated.
Serve pork immediately with warm tortillas, limes, avocado, pickled onions, and drizzle with any remaining salsa, if desired.

schema_metadata.keywords: po chuc, Yucatán-Style Grilled Pork Tacos, pork tacos, tacos

description: Make juicy grilled pork tacos inspired by Yucatán’s classic poc chuc, featuring smoky charred meat, a vibrant citrus salsa, and plenty of fresh toppings.
notes:
Notes: You can reduce the amount of habanero, but avoid swapping for a different chile, since the habanero’s fruitiness adds to the salsa’s flavor.

Make-ahead and storage: The grilled pork is best eaten right away, but the leftover pork and salsa can be refrigerated separately in airtight containers for up to 4 days.
author: Octavio Peña
